source: ** Kerry Rodden, Hilary Hutchinson, Xin Fu, "Measuring the User Experience
inclusion: the named standard for the value axis: the Goals to Signals to Metrics process, and the rule that a metric with no goal above it is dropped while raw counts become ratios, percentages or per-user averages

source: ** Nicole Forsgren, Margaret-Anne Storey, Chandra Maddila, Tom Zimmermann
inclusion: fixes the feasibility half of the scorecard: no single productivity or quality number is admissible on its own, so the axis reports the coverage of a constellation of dimensions instead of one index

source: ** DORA, *State of AI-assisted Software Development*, 2025 report, plus the
inclusion: the class-level evidence for why the gap matters: AI amplifies an existing weakness instead of neutralising it, and the cost lands on the reader as a verification tax
quality: vendor report published by the DORA research program itself, not peer-reviewed: a global survey plus a thematic read of 1,110 open-ended self-report responses from one company's engineers, so it carries a claim about the class of change and not a causal one about this repository; no academic index holds it - an `orx discover openalex` search for the report returns no record

source: ** `phuryn/pm-skills` — "PM Skills Marketplace", read through the GitHub API
inclusion: the prior art that splits along the same two axes and is MIT-licensed, and the intended-vs-implemented rule the line adopts as its feasibility standard
quality: community marketplace repository, not a measured source: the MIT licence, the star count and the plugin layout are checkable metadata, and the quality of the 69 skills is not measured here - three skill files were read, not 69

source: ** Xixun Lin et al., "LLM-based Agents Suffer from Hallucinations: A Survey
inclusion: establishes that agent hallucination is staged along the workflow, so a rule attached to one stage has to say which stage it covers instead of claiming to have solved hallucination

source: ** Kate Moran, Kelley Gordon, "How to Conduct a Heuristic Evaluation"
id: NN/g "How to Conduct a Heuristic Evaluation" (2023) and "Severity Ratings for Usability Problems"; W3C WCAG 2.2 REC and WCAG2Mobile Draft Note (2025-05-06); Umbrex Product Teardown Analysis; Appbot competitor review mining; Mind the Product kill criteria
inclusion: the standards the usability, competitive and triage axes cite: heuristic evaluation and its severity scale, WCAG 2.2 AA plus its mobile note, a comparison-basis teardown method, competitor review mining, and kill criteria
quality: practice literature rather than measurement: two NN/g method articles, two W3C documents of which one is an explicitly informative Draft Note, one consultancy teardown framework, one vendor article on review mining and one product-community article on kill criteria; they carry method weight only, and the NN/g method assumes several human evaluators where an agent is one rater

inclusion: the capability boundary of the two app-analysis MCPs the usability axis reads a running app with, which is what decides whether a UX claim can be re-run or stays a judgement
quality: vendor documentation plus registry metadata: the tool list and the version facts are checkable, and neither says how well an analysis actually reads a running app
